Rashi on Shabbat 25a:1:1.english: It is a positive commandment - For it implies: Rest on it.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:1:2.hebrew: ואין עשה - דבאש תשרופו דוחה יו"ט, דהוא לא תעשה ועשה. ואע"ג דהדלקת נר ביו"ט מלאכה המותרת היא — הואיל והבערת שאר קדשים שאין נהנין מהן נאסרין, גם זו לא יצא מן הכלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:1:2.english: And a positive [mitzva] does not - That [the positive mitzva of] “you shall burn [it] with fire” [would] override Yom Tov, which is a prohibition and a positive mitzva. And even though lighting a lamp on Yom Tov is a permitted labor, since the burning of other consecrated items—from which one may not derive benefit—is forbidden, this [lighting] too did not depart from the general rule.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:2:1.english: But on a weekday, it is permitted - To derive benefit from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:2:2.hebrew: מצוה לשרוף את התרומה שנטמאת - דדמיא לקדש, ועוד משום תקלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:2:2.english: [It is] a mitzvah to burn the terumah that became ritually impure - For it is similar to consecrated items, and furthermore, because of [the risk of] a mishap.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:3:1.english: “I have not burned of it” - It is written concerning the second tithe.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:3:2.hebrew: בטמא - בין שאני טמא, בין שהוא טמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:3:2.english: While impure - Whether I am impure, or whether it is impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:1.english: I do not exclude consecrated [items] - From this stringency.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:2.hebrew: שכן - יש בו חומרי פנקעכ"ס, וראוי גם לזו. חייבין עליו משום פיגול: שחט על מנת לאכול חוץ לזמנו, ואכל אפילו בזמנו; ומשום נותר: חוץ לזמנו ממש, ולא חשב מתחלה; וקרוי קרבן; ויש בו מעילה — ואף על גב שקדש (הנותר) לאכילת כהנים אין בהן מעילה, מ"מ תורת מעילה שייכא ביה: אם קדשי קדשים הן, יש בהן מעילה לפני זריקה לכל הנהנה מהן, ואם קדשים קלים הן, יש מעילה באימוריהן לאחר זריקת דמים — לאפוקי תרומה, דלית בה כלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:2.english: For - It has the stringencies of peh-nun-kuf, ayin-kaf-samekh [PNK ʿKS], and is fitting also for this [stringency]: One is liable regarding it on account of piggul: [where] one slaughtered [the offering] with the intention to eat [from it] beyond its [allotted] time, and one ate [from it] even within its [allotted] time; and on account of notar: [where it was left] beyond its [allotted] time in actuality, and one did not have [improper] intention at the outset; and it is called an offering [korban]; and it is subject to [the laws of] me’ila. And even though consecrated [meat] (that remains) for consumption by the priests is not subject to me’ila, nevertheless, the law of me’ila applies to it: If they are offerings of the highest sanctity [kodshei kodashim], they are subject to me’ila prior to the sprinkling [of the blood] for anyone who derives benefit from them; and if they are offerings of lesser sanctity [kodashim kalim], there is me’ila regarding their sacrificial portions [eimurin] after the sprinkling of the blood — to the exclusion of teruma, which is not subject to it at all.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:3.hebrew: וכרת - לאוכלה בטומאת הגוף, ותרומה במיתה בידי שמים — ימיו נקצרים, אבל אינו הולך ערירי:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:3.english: And karet - [Applies] to one who eats it in [a state of] bodily ritual impurity; whereas [for] teruma, [the penalty is] death at the hand of Heaven — his days are shortened, but he does not go childless.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:4.hebrew: אסור לאונן - ק"ו ממעשר, אבל תרומה מותרת לאונן — ביבמות בפרק הערל (יבמות דף ע:): זר זר ב' פעמים — זרות אמרתי לך ולא אנינות. אונן — כל זמן שלא נקבר מתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:6:4.english: Prohibited to an acute mourner - [This is derived by] an a fortiori argument from [second] tithe. But teruma is permitted to an acute mourner, [as taught] in [tractate] Yevamot, in chapter HaArel (Yevamot 70b): [The word] "non-priest" [zar is written] twice — "I spoke of non-priesthood [zarut], but not of acute mourning [aninut]." An acute mourner [onen is defined as someone] as long as his deceased [relative] has not been buried.

Rashi on Shabbat 25a:7:1.hebrew: מחפ"ז - מיתה בידי שמים לזר האוכלה, או כהן טמא. וחומש לזר האוכלה בשוגג, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד) "כי יאכל קדש בשגגה ויסף חמישיתו עליו". אבל קדש, משעה שיש היתר לכהנים כתרומה ויצא מידי מעילה, שוב אין חומש בשגגת אכילתו. ויש דמוקמי לה בחומשין דחומשא, ולא נהירא, דהא רבינן ביה חומש דחומש בהקדש בפרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף נד:):
Rashi on Shabbat 25a:7:1.english: Mem, ḥet, peh, zayin [Maḥpaz] - Death at the hand of Heaven for a non-priest who eats it, or [for] an impure priest [who eats it]; and a fifth for a non-priest who eats it unwittingly, as it is written (Leviticus 22:14): “And if a person eats of a sacred item unwittingly, then he shall add its fifth unto it.” But [with regard to] a consecrated item, from the time that there is permission for the priests [to eat it], like teruma, and it is released from [the laws of] misuse [me’ila], there is no longer a fifth [incurred] for eating it unwittingly. And some interpret it as [referring to] a fifth of a fifth, but this is not plausible, as we derive a fifth of a fifth with regard to consecrated property in chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 54b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:1:1.hebrew: ה"ל יו"ט עשה כו' - וא"ת: הנך אמוראי דלעיל דסברי דיו"ט לא תעשה גרידא — נילף מהכא דלא דחי עשה את ל"ת? וכי האי גוונא פריך בפ"ק דיבמות (דף ו.). ושמא מיכן לא נילף, לפי שיכול לעשות אחר יו"ט [ת"י]:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:1:1.english: And Yom Tov is a positive mitzva, etc. - And if you will say: [According to] those Amoraim above who hold that Yom Tov is merely a prohibition, let us derive from here that a positive mitzva does not override a prohibition! And in a similar manner, [the Gemara] challenges in the first chapter of Yevamot (6a). And perhaps from here we cannot derive [this], because he can perform [the mitzva] after Yom Tov. [Tosafot Yeshanim]

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:1.hebrew: הא בחול שפיר דמי מ"ט כו' - תימה: מהיכא תיתי דתרומה טמאה אסורה בהנאה, דבעי "מ"ט"? אי ממעשר הקל, כדמשמע בסמוך — איכא למיפרך: מה למעשר שכן הד"ס ט"ב, כדפריך בהערל (יבמות דף עד:)! וליכא למימר דהוה אסרינן ליה משום דאיקרי קדש, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד) "ונתן לכהן את הקדש", או משום דהוקשה לקדשים, כדאמר במעילה בפרק הנהנה (דף יט.): "דקדש אקשי רחמנא לתרומה", וקדש גופיה אסור בהנאה כשניטמא — אפילו אותו קדש שהיה מותר בהנאה קודם, כמו שלמים — נפקא לן שפיר מק"ו דמעשר או מהיקשא דמעשר, כדאמר בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כד.); דא"כ, מאי פריך: "ומה ראית? ואימא ממנו אתא למעוטי קדש ולא תרומה"? ואם נמעט קדש, מהיכא תיתי איסור תרומה?! וי"ל, דהוה גמרינן תרומה מדאיתקש לבכורים ובכורים למעשר, כדאמרינן בהערל (יבמות דף מג:); ולקמן לא סמיך אק"ו, אלא אהיקשא סמיך. ומיהו קדש אתי שפיר בק"ו ממעשר, כדאמרי' בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כד.), וליכא למיפרך: "שכן הד"ס ט"ב", דכולהו איתנהו בקדש, בר מוידוי. ואר"ת, דמוידוי לא שייך למיפרך, דלא שייך וידוי גבי קדש; אבל בתרומה שייך, דהא אגב מעשר מתודה נמי אתרומה, כדאמר: "וגם נתתיו ללוי" — זו תרומה, ואין לה וידוי בפני עצמה. וא"ת: אכתי היכי יליף בק"ו קדש ממעשר? הא איכא למיפרך: מה למעשר שכן טעון כסף צורה, כדפריך בפרק בתרא דמכות (דף יז:)! ואור"י, דלא שייך האי פירכא אלא דוקא גבי חוץ לחומה, כדהתם, דבעי למילף דאוכל תודה או שלמים חוץ לחומה דלוקה ממעשר. ואם תאמר: הכא אסרינן הסקה והדלקה באיסורי הנאה, וערלה דאסורה בהנאה ושרי ליהנות בשעת ביעור, כדאמר בפרק כל שעה (פסחים כז:) ולא משכח התם עצים לרבנן דאסורים אלא בשרשיפא? וצריך לדחות ולומר, דשמן ובשר ותבואה חשיבי בעין טפי בשעת היסק מעצים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:1.english: "Rather, on a weekday it is permitted; what is the reason, etc." - It is astonishing: From where would it be derived that impure teruma is forbidden from [any] benefit, such that [the Gemara] asks: "What is the reason" [that on a weekday it is permitted]? If [one suggests that it is derived] from the lenient [case of second] tithe, as is implied nearby — one can refute [this]: What [is true] of tithe [is] that it has [the five stringencies represented by the acronym] hadas tet-beit (הד״ס ט״ב: that it requires being brought to Jerusalem, a declaration, is forbidden to an acute mourner, is forbidden in ritual impurity, and requires removal), as [the Gemara] refutes in [Perek] Ha'arel (Yevamot 74b)! And it cannot be said that we would forbid it because it is called "holy" [kodesh], as it is written: "And he shall give the holy thing to the priest" (Leviticus 22:14), or because it is juxtaposed to consecrated items, as [the Gemara] says in Meilah in Perek HaNeheneh (19a) that "the Merciful One juxtaposed sacred items to teruma," and consecrated items themselves are forbidden from benefit when they become impure — even that consecrated item that was permitted for benefit beforehand, such as a peace-offering — [which] is indeed derived for us from an a fortiori inference [kal vaḥomer] from tithe, or from the juxtaposition to tithe, as [the Gemara] says in Perek Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 24a) — for if so, why does [the Gemara later] ask: "And what did you see [to exclude teruma]? Say [instead that] 'from it' came to exclude consecrated items and not teruma"? But if we exclude consecrated items, from where would the prohibition of teruma be derived?! And it can be answered that we would derive teruma from the fact that it is juxtaposed to first fruits [bikkurim], and first fruits to [second] tithe, as we say in [Perek] Ha'arel (Yevamot 43b [73b]); and later [in the Gemara], it does not rely on an a fortiori inference, but rather it relies on the juxtaposition. However, consecrated items are properly derived through an a fortiori inference from tithe, as we say in Perek Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 24a), and one cannot refute [it by arguing] that [tithe has the stringencies of] hadas tet-beit, for all of them apply to consecrated items, except for the declaration [viddui]. And Rabbeinu Tam said that from the declaration, it is not relevant to refute [the inference], because a declaration is not applicable to consecrated items; but regarding teruma it is relevant, for along with [second] tithe one also confesses over teruma, as [the verse] states: "And I have also given it to the Levite" (Deuteronomy 26:13) — this is teruma — yet it does not have a declaration of its own. And if you say: Still, how does [the Gemara] derive consecrated items from tithe through an a fortiori inference? But isn't there [another] refutation: What [is true] of tithe [is] that it requires coined silver, as [the Gemara] refutes in the last chapter of Makkot (17b)! And the Ri answered that this refutation is relevant only specifically regarding [eating] outside the wall [of Jerusalem], as [in the case] there, where [the Gemara] seeks to derive that one who eats a thanks-offering or a peace-offering outside the wall is flogged, from tithe. And if you say: Here, we prohibit heating and kindling with items forbidden from benefit, yet orlah, which is forbidden from benefit, is permitted to be benefited from at the time of its destruction, as [the Gemara] says in Perek Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 27b), and [the Gemara] does not find prohibited wood according to the Rabbis except in [the case of sitting on] a stool? And it must be dismissed and answered that oil, meat, and grain are considered more tangible in substance at the time of kindling than wood.

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:2.hebrew: כך אתה מצווה לשרוף את התרומה - פי' בקונטרס: משום דלא ליתי בה לידי תקלה. לפי טעם זה, נראה דלאו דוקא שריפה, אלא ה"ה שאר ביעור; וכ"פ בהדיא באלו עוברין. ול"נ, דבסוף תמורה (דף לג:) קתני תרומה טמאה בהדי הנשרפין, וקתני התם: "הנשרפין לא יקברו". ע"כ נראה דשריפה דוקא — משום דדמיא לקדש ומדרבנן, א"נ מדאורייתא מדאיקרי קדש. ואם תאמר: דאמר בספ"ק דפסחים (דף כ:) גבי תרומה טמאה שתעשה זילוף, הא תנן בתמורה: "הראוי לקבורה קבורה", פירוש: כגון משקין? ויש לומר: דלא קאי אלא אערלה וכלאי הכרם, ולא אתרומה, דשריא בהנאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:2.english: "So too, you are commanded to burn the terumah" - The Kuntres explained: [It is] so that one will not come to a mishap through it. According to this reason, it would seem that burning is not specifically [required], but rather the same applies to any other [manner of] destruction; and so he [Rashi] explained explicitly in [the chapter] Elu Ovrin. However, this does not appear [correct] to us, for at the end of Temurah (33b), it teaches ritually impure terumah among those [items] that are burned, and it teaches there: "Those that are burned shall not be buried." Therefore, it appears that burning is specifically [required] — because it is similar to consecrated items [kodesh], and [this is] rabbinically; or alternatively, by Torah law, because it is called "holy" [kodesh]. And if you say: But [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Pesachim (20b) regarding ritually impure terumah that it should be used for sprinkling [ziluf] — yet didn't we learn in the Mishnah in Temurah: "That which is fit for burial [shall undergo] burial" (explanation: such as liquids)? And one can say: That [ruling] applies only to orlah and diverse kinds in a vineyard [kil'ei hakerem], but not to terumah, which is permitted for benefit.

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:3.hebrew: אחת תרומה טמאה ואחת תרומה טהורה - ואף על גב דדריש רבי אליעזר (בפורות דף לד. וסם): אחת תרומה טהורה ואחת תלויה, יניחנה במקום המוצנע ולא במקום התורפה, דאסור לגרום לה טומאה — התם דריש "משמרת תרומותי", משמע שתי תרומות צריכות שימור, דהיינו טהורה ותלויה; והכא דריש מלך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:2:3.english: One ritually impure teruma and one ritually pure teruma - And even though Rabbi Eliezer expounds (in Bekhorot 34a and there [in Terumot 8:8]) [that the verse refers to] one ritually pure teruma and one in suspense [teluyah, ruling that] one must place it in a concealed place and not in an exposed place, for it is forbidden to cause ritual impurity to it — there, he expounds "the charge of My terumot" [mishmeret terumotai], which implies that two terumot require safeguarding [shimur], namely, [definitely] pure and in suspense; but here, [the Gemara] expounds from [the word] "to you" [lekha].

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:1.hebrew: שכן פנק עכ"ס - תימה, דמצי לאחשובי נמי דחמירי קדשים מתרומה בהא: העריב שמשו — אוכל בתרומה; הביא כפרתו — אוכל בקדשים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:1.english: "For PeNaK AKhaS" - It is puzzling, as [the Gemara] could also have reckoned that consecrated items are more stringent than teruma in this: [Once] his sun has set, he may eat teruma; [once] he has brought his atonement offering, he may eat consecrated items.

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:2.hebrew: פגול - היינו חישב לאוכלו חוץ למקומו, ובכלל זה הוי אוכל חוץ לחומה דלוקה בקדשים. ונותר — היינו חישב לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו, והוי נותר בכלל זה. והוי האי פיגול ונותר כי ההוא ד"אם עון פיגול הוא הרי כבר נאמר לא יחשב, ואם עון נותר כו'" (פסחים דף טז:), ולא כמו פיגול שבכל הש"ס, דקרי פיגול דחישב לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו, דהיינו נותר דהכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:2.english: Piggul - That is, [one who] had intention to eat it outside its [designated] area; and included in this [category] is one who eats [sacrificial meat] outside the wall, who incurs lashes in [the case of] consecrated items. And "notar" — that is, [one who] had intention to eat it beyond its [designated] time, and [actual] notar is included in this [category]. And this [use of the terms] piggul and notar is like that [baraita]: "If [it atones for] the sin of piggul, behold it has already been stated: 'It shall not be credited'; and if [it atones for] the sin of notar, etc." (Pesachim 16b) — and not like [the term] piggul throughout the Talmud, which calls [only one who] had intention to eat it beyond its [designated] time "piggul," which is [what is termed] "notar" here.

Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:3.hebrew: כרת - שאינו מגיע לששים שנה, שהוא מיתת כל אדם, כדמשמע בשילהי מ"ק (דף כח. ושם), דאמר התם: רב יוסף, כי הוה בר שיתין שנין, עבד יומא טבא לרבנן; אמר: "השתא נפקי לי מכרת". א"ל אביי: "נהי דנפק מר מכרת דשני, מכרת דיומי מי נפק מר?". פירוש: כדאמר התם: מת ביום א' — מיתה של זעם; שנים — מיתה של בהלה; שלשה — מיתה של כרת. ומיתה בידי שמים אין לה זמן קבוע, אלא שמת בשביל עון זה, אפי' אין בידו עון אחר; ואפי' למ"ד (לקמן שבת דף כה.) יש מיתה בלא חטא, בשביל עון זה יקצרו ימיו. ומיהו בירושל' קאמר דכרת אינו מגיע לחמשים, ומפיק לה מ"אל תכריתו את שבט הקהתי וגו' וזאת עשו להם וחיו". פי' אמרה תורה: עשו להם תקנה שלא ימותו בעבודתן קודם חמשים, וכתיב "אל תכריתו", משמע: כרת היינו שמת קודם חמישים. ומיתה האמורה בתורה דקאמר התם, היינו שמת עד ששים, דכתיב: "במדבר הזה יתמו ושם ימותו", ולא נגזרה גזירה אלא על בני עשרים שימותו קודם ארבעים, וקרי לה מיתה. אבל זרעו — אומר ריב"א דאין בכרת אלא בהנהו דכתיב בהו "ערירי". ואין נראה לר"ת, דהא בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נה.) קאמר: "ערירי דכתב רחמנא גבי דודתו למה לי? לכדרבא כו'". ואי אין זרעו נכרת אלא דוקא בהנהו דכתיב "ערירי", מאי קבעי? והא דלא קאמר במועד קטן (דף כח. ושם): "נהי דנפק מר מכרת דשני, מכרת דבני מי נפק מר?" — התם מיירי כשאין לו בנים קטנים, ודוקא קטנים נענשים בעון אביהם ולא גדולים, כדמשמע בפירקין (דף לב:). ומיהו קשה, דבתורת כהנים ממעט אשת אח מן האם מכרת, מדכתיב: "אשת אחיו נדה היא" — מה נדה יש לה היתר, אף אשת אח דיש לה היתר, דהיינו מן האב דשריא כשאין לה בנים; ובכולי הש"ס משמע דיש בה כרת כמו בשאר עריות, דהא מני לה גבי חמש עשרה נשים פוטרות צרותיהן! ולפירוש ריב"א אתי שפיר, דמצינן למימר דממעט לה מערירי, ואין להאריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 25a:6:3.english: Karet - [This means] that one does not reach sixty years [of age], which is [the threshold of] the ordinary death of all people, as is implied at the end of Moed Katan (28a and ibid.), where it says there: When Rav Yosef was sixty years old, he made a festive celebration for the Sages. He said: "Now I have emerged from [liability to] karet." Abaye said to him: "Granted that the Master has emerged from the karet of years, has the Master emerged from the karet of days?" Explanation: As [the Gemara] says there: If one dies [after an illness of] one day, it is a death of wrath; [after] two [days], it is a death of panic; [after] three, it is a death of karet. And death at the hand of Heaven has no fixed time [age]; rather, he dies on account of this sin, even if he has no other sin in his hand; and even according to the one who says (below, Shabbat 55b [printed: 25a]) that there is death without sin, on account of this sin his days will be shortened. However, in the Yerushalmi [Bikkurim 2:1] it says that [one liable to] karet does not reach fifty [years of age], and it derives this from [the verse]: "Do not cut off [al takhritu] the tribe of the families of the Kohathites, etc., but do this to them, that they may live [and not die]" (Numbers 4:18–19). Explanation: The Torah said, make an arrangement for them so that they do not die during their service before [age] fifty [since Levites serve until fifty]; and it is written "Do not cut off [al takhritu]," which implies that karet means dying before fifty. And the "death" mentioned in the Torah that is stated there [in the Yerushalmi as death at the hand of Heaven] means dying by [age] sixty, as it is written: "In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die" (Numbers 14:35); and the decree was issued only against those twenty years old [and above], that they should die within forty [years, i.e., by age sixty], and [the Torah] calls this "death." However, regarding his offspring, Riva says that [their being cut off] is not included in karet except in those [cases] where "childless" [ariri] is written. And this does not appear correct to Rabbeinu Tam, for in the chapter [entitled] "Haba Al Yevamto" (Yevamot 55a), [the Gemara] says: "Why did the Merciful One write 'childless' with regard to his aunt? For that which Rabba taught, etc." Now, if his offspring were not cut off except specifically in those [cases] where "childless" is written, what was [the Gemara] asking? And as for that which [Abaye] did not say in Moed Katan (28a and ibid.), "Granted that the Master has emerged from the karet of years, has the Master emerged from the karet of children?", there it is dealing with a case where he had no minor children, and it is specifically minor children who are punished for the sin of their father, but not adult children, as is implied in our chapter (32b). However, there is a difficulty, for in Torat Kohanim [Sifra, Kedoshim 11:11] it excludes a maternal brother's wife from karet, from that which is written: "It is his brother's wife; she is impurity [niddah]" (Leviticus 20:21) — just as a menstruant [niddah] has [a manner of] permissibility [after immersing], so too a brother's wife who has [a manner of] permissibility, which is a paternal [brother's wife], who is permitted when she has no children [through yibbum; thus excluding a maternal brother's wife, who is never permitted]. Yet throughout the entire Talmud it is implied that [intercourse with] her carries karet just like all other forbidden relations [arayot], for [the Mishnah in Yevamot 2a] counts her among the fifteen women who exempt their co-wives! But according to Riva's explanation it works out well, for we can say that it only excludes her from [the punishment of being] childless [ariri]. And there is no need to elaborate.
